chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Musanna al-Hannat, from Abi Baseer, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Chess and backgammon are both al-maysir (gambling).'

key_terms.الْمَيْسِرُ: Gambling (specifically the pre-Islamic form of dice gambling, used here as a category for games of chance)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on chess and backgammon according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from al-Kafi establishes the legal ruling for chess and backgammon by classifying them as 'al-maysir' (gambling), thereby rendering them forbidden (haram) in Islamic jurisprudence. It attributes this classification directly to Amir al-Mu'minin (Imam Ali, peace be upon him), linking the physical games to the broader Quranic concept of gambling and dice-throwing. This ruling is significant in Shia fiqh as it extends the prohibition of 'maysir' beyond mere monetary wagering to include the games themselves due to their association with distraction and chance.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Musny Al Hannat, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The chess and the dice, are both (classified as) the gambling’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn abu Najran from Muthanna’ al-Hannat from abu Basir who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ’Amir al-Mu’minin has said, ‘Chess and dice are al- Maysir (gambling).”’
